bibl.title: Sensory representation of an auditory cued tactile stimulus in the posterior parietal cortex of the mouse

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how an association cortex represents a tactile stimulus, the sound that announces it, and its absence
span.quote: Sensory association cortices receive diverse inputs with their role in representing and integrating multi-sensory content remaining unclear.

span.label: how whisker-based tactile stimuli are represented in the microcircuits of posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: While visual and auditory processing in PPC during behaviour have been extensively studied in mice 7 , 15 , 17 , 18 , 25 , 26 , we know little about how whisker-based tactile stimuli are represented in the neuronal microcircuits of PPC.

span.label: layer 2/3 neurons discriminate not only texture graininess but the presence against the omission of the cued touch, and may encode expectancy
span.quote: Notably, altering the flow of sensory events through omission of the cued texture touch elicited large responses in a subset of neurons hardly responsive to or even inhibited by the tactile stimuli. Hence, PPC neurons were able to discriminate not only tactile stimulus features (i.e., texture graininess) but also between the presence and omission of the texture stimulus.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Hence, PPC neurons were able to discriminate not only tactile stimulus features (i.e., texture graininess) but also between the presence and omission of the texture stimulus.

span.label: stimulus-omission responses in posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: More interestingly, we found that about 30% of trial-active PPC neurons responded to the omission of the texture touch that always arrived after the auditory cues.

span.label: two-photon-calcium-imaging
span.quote: We performed in vivo calcium imaging of layer 2/3 PPC neurons (at 150 to 220 µm depth) through a cranial window using YC-Nano140, a genetically encoded ratiometric calcium indicator that reliably reports action potential discharge 27 (Fig. 2A ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The looming-like cue and the ensuing touch inhibit a subset of PPC neurons; when the expected touch fails to arrive these neurons are released from that inhibition, which is why omission produces a large response in cells that texture touch suppresses.
span.quote: Interestingly, 55.3% of the Catch-responsive neurons were non-responsive or even suppressed during texture presentation trials, suggesting that they were inhibited by the looming-like auditory cues and/or a subsequent texture touch, but relieved from inhibition when the texture was absent.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Thalamic LP/Po input to PPC is gated by top-down feedback, plausibly from the frontal eye field, which activates local inhibitory circuits and supplies the prediction signal of a predictive-coding scheme, so a violated prediction emerges as the omission response.
span.quote: This could be in turn modulated through the activation of local inhibitory circuits by top-down feedback, potentially from the FEF, providing the prediction signal in the proposed framework of predictive coding 53 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A looming sound signals an approaching source and thereby creates an expectancy of an imminent touch event, which is the expectancy the omission then violates.
span.quote: Looming sounds have been proposed to represent the approach of the sound source in the context of threat detection, either in the form of an attack or collision, and can evoke rapid attention capture and expectancy 38 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Omission-responsive PPC neurons act as mismatch reporters that forward information about unexpected changes in sensory flow to prefrontal cortex, FEF and LP, areas allocating attention.
span.quote: Hence these neurons could function as reporters of mismatch signals, which could reliably convey information about unexpected changes in sensory flow to the prefrontal cortex, FEF and LP (the mouse equivalent of the pulvinar), brain areas that are implicated in the allocation of attentional resources 9 .

span.label: the looming-like sound of the approaching stage may itself signal an incoming touch, so the omission response could be an expectancy that the touch does not satisfy
span.quote: Apart from one neuron (onset 120 ms after the texture stop tone) the others displayed onset times well before the translation stage came to rest (onset 580 ± 65 ms before texture stop tone, n = 18 neurons). This indicates that the Catch-trial responses were not due to the stop auditory tone and could potentially represent an expectancy response that can be further enhanced by whisking.

span.label: two populations contribute: some neurons already respond before any tactile experience, others are recruited only after sound and touch have been coupled
span.quote: Our results suggest that while looming-like auditory cues alone can evoke responses in the PPC, coupling with tactile stimuli enhances this response and further recruits more neurons within PPC that can report subsequent texture-touch omissions.

span.label: the thalamic lateral posterior nucleus and the posterior nucleus are the main thalamic input to this area and a candidate source of the omission response
span.quote: LP, along with the posterior nucleus Po, is the main source of thalamic input to the PPC, which does not receive any direct input from primary sensory thalamus 2 , 52 . Hence, LP/Po could be a potential source for the Catch-trial responses that we have observed in layer 2/3 of the PPC. This could be in turn modulated through the activation of local inhibitory circuits by top-down feedback, potentially from the FEF, providing the prediction signal in the proposed framework of predictive coding

span.label: the responses could report mismatch to frontal and thalamic areas that allocate attention
span.quote: Hence these neurons could function as reporters of mismatch signals, which could reliably convey information about unexpected changes in sensory flow to the prefrontal cortex, FEF and LP (the mouse equivalent of the pulvinar), brain areas that are implicated in the allocation of attentional resources

span.label: Too few Catch-responsive neurons were recorded to establish whether the pre-existing, silenced and emergent subsets are genuinely distinct functional groups.
span.quote: Due to the low numbers of Catch-responsive neurons detected, however, more data would be required to determine if these three subsets of neurons represent functionally distinct groups.

span.label: The looming-like auditory cue is inherent to the stimulation apparatus and could not be eliminated as a confound.
span.quote: Unfortunately, we were unable to remove the looming-like auditory cue, as it is an integral part of the texture presentation apparatus.

span.label: The linear SVM decoding gives only a lower bound on the information carried by the population.
span.quote: This approach provides a lower bound on the actual information carried by the population, and does not preclude that more advanced methods cannot extract additional information.

span.label: the looming auditory cue could not be removed because it is generated by the stimulus apparatus itself
span.quote: Unfortunately, we were unable to remove the looming-like auditory cue, as it is an integral part of the texture presentation apparatus.

span.label: the three subsets of omission-responsive neurons are named but explicitly not claimed as functionally distinct groups, for want of numbers
span.quote: Due to the low numbers of Catch-responsive neurons detected, however, more data would be required to determine if these three subsets of neurons represent functionally distinct groups.

span.label: texture discrimination was weak, which the authors attribute to naive animals with no training and no context attached to graininess
span.quote: Few PPC neurons (7.2%) were able to discriminate the two distinct textures presented. This low discrimination power is not surprising as the experimental sessions were only the second time that the naïve mice were exposed to these textures (the first being setting the texture stop position, prior to imaging start). No explicit association of a relevant context to the texture graininess as stimulus feature or any reinforcement training had been applied.

span.label: an alternative reading remains open in which pre-existing neurons are purely sound-driven and only begin reporting omission after coupling
span.quote: It is also plausible that the pre-existing Catch-responsive neurons are purely looming sound responsive in the Catch-only trials and start to report texture omission only after coupling with texture touch.

span.label: omission responses are known from mismatch and oddball work, but with stimulus paradigms different from this one
span.quote: Indeed stimulus-omission responses have also been described in the auditory 42 , 43 and visual systems 44 – 46 in the context of mismatch negativity (MMN) and oddball responses. However, the stimulus presentation paradigms employed in MMN are different compared to those used in our study.

span.label: A linear SVM classifier (via the scikit-learn python package) is imported as a population read-out model for neural activity, and justified as an operation biological neurons could plausibly implement.
span.quote: A linear SVM computes a simple thresholded weighted sum of inputs, an operation that is plausibly implementable by actual biological neurons; high linear classifier performance has been suggested as an indicator that the neural representation is such that it can be easily readout by downstream neurons 62 .

span.label: looming responsiveness of multimodal neurons, carried into the mouse as the interpretive frame for the cue
span.quote: Apart from one neuron (onset 120 ms after the texture stop tone) the others displayed onset times well before the translation stage came to rest (onset 580 ± 65 ms before texture stop tone, n = 18 neurons). This indicates that the Catch-trial responses were not due to the stop auditory tone and could potentially represent an expectancy response that can be further enhanced by whisking.

span.label: a linear support vector machine used as a readout model on single-trial population activity
span.quote: As a complement to the ideal observer ROC analysis, we trained a linear support vector machine (SVM) classifier to decode texture graininess and texture omission from single-trial population activity, on a frame by frame basis. This simple readout model could effectively decode texture graininess and texture omission during the touch-stimulus window with about 55% and 70% accuracy, respectively (Fig. 4E ). The decoding accuracy was improved when the mean of the touch-stimulus window was used (60.1 ± 3.1% for texture graininess; 73.1 ± 4.3% for texture omission).

span.label: every whisker except the one aligned to the imaged barrel column TRIMMED, with the remaining whisker's location mapped by intrinsic optical signal
span.quote: to avoid the activation of surrounding whiskers, all whiskers except the

span.label: neurons EXCLUDED from the Catch-responsive class when their average calcium transient fell by more than 50 per cent
span.quote: In order to avoid erroneously classifying cue-responsive neurons with large transients as Catch-responsive, neurons were excluded

span.label: Catch-trial responses → whisking
span.note: TESTED AND NOT SUPPORTED: Catch-trial responses were observed both in the ABSENCE and PRESENCE of whisking, indicating they were NOT SOLELY DEPENDENT ON WHISKING. Note the hedge the authors chose - 'not solely' leaves a contributory role open, so this is a bounded negative and not a flat denial. No edge type can express either.
span.quote: We next verified whether the Catch-trial responses might reflect an efferent copy of a motor command such as whisking because the PPC has strong reciprocal connections with the motor and premotor cortices 1 – 3 . Catch-trial responses were observed both in the absence and presence of whisking behaviour (see Methods) during the touch-stimulus window, indicating that they were not solely dependent on whisking

span.label: a Catch-trial is not a control in the usual sense but the stimulus of interest - everything is present except the touch, so the response measures what the ABSENCE does
span.quote: To determine the influence of these stage-generated auditory cues, we interleaved the texture trials with ‘Catch’-trials, in which textures were omitted but with all auditory cues present (start and stop tones), including the sounds generated by the stage translation

span.label: the region called PPC here is identified by intrinsic-signal boundaries and then VALIDATED by tracing its inputs and outputs, rather than assumed from coordinates
span.quote: In four mice, we carried out retrograde and anterograde labelling experiments with tracer injections targeted to LPtA. The resulting labelling patterns validated that this region receives axonal projections from known PPC input sites (Fig. 1D ), particularly the thalamic lateral posterior nucleus LP (Fig. 1H,I ) and premotor cortex M2 (Fig. 1E-F ), as well as sends its axons to known PPC output sites, including M2, the dorsal striatum (Fig. 1E–G ) and LP (Fig. 1H,I ) 15 , 32 . Hence, we identify this region between barrel cortex and V1 as part of PPC

span.label: the auditory cue is not a designed stimulus but a by-product of the apparatus, measured after the fact and confirmed to be looming-like by recording at the animal's head position
span.quote: We confirmed that the auditory cue generated by the stage translation was indeed looming-like by performing sound recordings at the location corresponding to the head of the head-fixed mouse

span.label: response classes here are outputs of a general linear model fit to calcium traces, so cue-responsive, touch-responsive, mixed and suppressed are model categories rather than observed types
span.quote: Using a general linear model (GLM) to fit neuronal calcium traces, we classified the trial-active neurons (n = 126) as cue-responsive (22.2%), touch-responsive (11.9%), mixed-responsive (11.9%) and suppressed (17.5%) based on the dynamics of their calcium responses to the trial period; the remaining 36.5% of ‘unclassified’ active neurons responded neither to auditory cues nor to texture presentation

span.label: the omission response was present on the SECOND trial the animal ever experienced, which is what makes it a fact about the cue rather than about learning
span.quote: Furthermore, for all 4 FOVs the first Catch-trial was presented as the second trial in the sequence of trials, suggesting that the PPC is able to rapidly encode the omission of the auditory-cued tactile stimulus.

span.label: builds-on → prior reports of a temporal associative role of PPC (cited as refs 19, 20)
span.quote: These findings are in line with the recently reported temporal associative role of PPC 19 , 20 , which could be due to its long timescale population dynamics allowing the combination of events separated in time 26 .

span.label: extends → the reported temporal associative role of posterior parietal cortex in encoding past choices and outcomes
span.quote: Hence, neurons within PPC are capable of representing a change in sensory flow, in a manner that is both rapid and stable. This could be essential for the role of PPC in spatial processing, navigation and the allocation of attention, allowing it to rapidly update changes in sensory information in particular to objects that are close to the body.

span.label: distinguishes-from → mismatch negativity and oddball paradigms, whose stimulus presentation differs from this one
span.quote: Indeed stimulus-omission responses have also been described in the auditory 42 , 43 and visual systems 44 – 46 in the context of mismatch negativity (MMN) and oddball responses. However, the stimulus presentation paradigms employed in MMN are different compared to those used in our study.

span.label: builds-on → mismatch responses reported in mouse V1 when visual flow is uncoupled from self-initiated locomotion
span.quote: More recently, mismatch responses have been reported in mouse V1 47 , 48 when visual flow is not correlated with self-initiated locomotion. These mismatch signals were also present in LP inputs to layer 1 of V1 49 , and mediated by a balance of motor-related excitation and visually driven inhibition during coupled sensorimotor experience 50 , 51 . While our stimulus paradigm does not involve a conflict with a self-initiated stimulus response, such as visual feedback from locomotion, it nonetheless incorporates a behaviourally salient stimulus (the looming auditory cue) that when coupled with tactile stimuli, can lead to a rapid encoding of omissions in the coupled sensory flow.

span.label: supports → the proposal that looming sounds signal an approaching source and evoke attention capture and expectancy
span.quote: Apart from one neuron (onset 120 ms after the texture stop tone) the others displayed onset times well before the translation stage came to rest (onset 580 ± 65 ms before texture stop tone, n = 18 neurons). This indicates that the Catch-trial responses were not due to the stop auditory tone and could potentially represent an expectancy response that can be further enhanced by whisking.

span.label: Catch —distinct-from→ texture
span.note: everything is held present except the texture - the start and stop tones and the stage sounds all remain - so what is measured is the effect of an ABSENCE
span.quote: To determine the influence of these stage-generated auditory cues, we interleaved the texture trials with ‘Catch’-trials, in which textures were omitted but with all auditory cues present (start and stop tones), including the sounds generated by the stage translation

span.label: looming —is-a→ auditory cue
span.note: the property was not designed in but MEASURED afterwards, by recording at the animal's head position
span.quote: We confirmed that the auditory cue generated by the stage translation was indeed looming-like by performing sound recordings at the location corresponding to the head of the head-fixed mouse

span.label: auditory cue —causes→ Catch
span.note: DECOUPLED IN TIME: Catch-only sessions in fresh animals separate the sound from any tactile experience
span.quote: To verify this possibility, we presented an additional 3 naïve mice first with Catch-trials only, effectively decoupling the auditory cues from tactile stimuli.

span.label: stop tone —distinct-from→ Catch
span.note: CRITERION: the responses begin about 580 ms BEFORE the stage stops, so the stop tone cannot be what drives them
span.quote: Apart from one neuron (onset 120 ms after the texture stop tone) the others displayed onset times well before the translation stage came to rest (onset 580 ± 65 ms before texture stop tone, n = 18 neurons). This indicates that the Catch-trial responses were not due to the stop auditory tone and could potentially represent an expectancy response that can be further enhanced by whisking.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE SPAN TESTS THE RELATION AND REPORTS THAT IT FAILS) · whisking —causes→ Catch
span.note: RETRACTED: THE SPAN TESTS THE RELATION AND REPORTS THAT IT FAILS. The edge is `whisking --causes--> Catch`. The span sets up the hypothesis - 'We next verified whether the Catch-trial responses might reflect an efferent copy of a motor command such as whisking BECAUSE the PPC has strong reciprocal connections with the motor and premotor cortices' - and then reports the test: 'Catch-trial responses were observed BOTH IN THE ABSENCE AND PRESENCE of whisking behaviour ..., INDICATING THAT THEY WERE NOT SOLELY DEPENDENT ON WHISKING.' The `because` introduces the MOTIVATION for testing, not a finding, and the finding is negative. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): housed below. FIFTH polarity instance in this pass. — PARTIAL: whisking enhances the response but the response occurs without it, so it is not an efferent copy alone
span.quote: We next verified whether the Catch-trial responses might reflect an efferent copy of a motor command such as whisking because the PPC has strong reciprocal connections with the motor and premotor cortices 1 – 3 . Catch-trial responses were observed both in the absence and presence of whisking behaviour (see Methods) during the touch-stimulus window, indicating that they were not solely dependent on whisking

span.label: whisking —distinct-from→ Catch
span.note: and the ONSET TIME does not differ with whisking, which is the stronger version of the same argument
span.quote: However, the onset time of the Catch-trial responses (from trial start) were comparable in the presence and absence of whisking (Fig. 3E ; Catch-response onset time: whisking 3.7 ± 0.1 s, non-whisking 3.8 ± 0.1 s; p = 0.56, n = 34 Catch-responsive neurons in 17.3 ± 0.1% and 82.7 ± 0.1% of Catch-trials respectively, Wilcoxon signed paired test).

span.label: GLM —operationalised-as→ auditory cue
span.note: the response categories are model outputs, not observed cell types
span.quote: Using a general linear model (GLM) to fit neuronal calcium traces, we classified the trial-active neurons (n = 126) as cue-responsive (22.2%), touch-responsive (11.9%), mixed-responsive (11.9%) and suppressed (17.5%) based on the dynamics of their calcium responses to the trial period; the remaining 36.5% of ‘unclassified’ active neurons responded neither to auditory cues nor to texture presentation

span.label: ROC —operationalised-as→ texture
span.note: and the same test shows omission is discriminated by more than twice as many neurons as graininess
span.quote: We carried out an ROC analysis to identify the fraction of neurons that could significantly discriminate between the two presented textures as well as the fraction of neurons that could discriminate between texture-presentation and Catch-trials (compared to shuffled controls, Methods; example traces in Fig. 4B ). Among the trial-active PPC neurons 7.2% (9/126) discriminated between the graininess of the presented textures whereas 17.5% (22/126) discriminated between texture presence and omission

span.label: SVM —operationalised-as→ omission
span.quote: As a complement to the ideal observer ROC analysis, we trained a linear support vector machine (SVM) classifier to decode texture graininess and texture omission from single-trial population activity, on a frame by frame basis. This simple readout model could effectively decode texture graininess and texture omission during the touch-stimulus window with about 55% and 70% accuracy, respectively (Fig. 4E ). The decoding accuracy was improved when the mean of the touch-stimulus window was used (60.1 ± 3.1% for texture graininess; 73.1 ± 4.3% for texture omission).

span.label: RETRACTED (AN IMAGING METHOD AND ONE OF THE LANDMARKS IT LOCATES) · IOS —operationalised-as→ V1
span.note: RETRACTED: AN IMAGING METHOD AND ONE OF THE LANDMARKS IT LOCATES. The edge is `IOS --operationalised-as--> V1`, which reads back as: IOS is measured as V1. The span: 'In order to localize PPC in mice, WE PERFORMED INTRINSIC OPTICAL SIGNAL (IOS) IMAGING to visualize THE BOUNDARIES BETWEEN the gamma-barrel column in the mouse whisker barrel cortex AND THE PRIMARY VISUAL CORTEX V1'. V1 is one of two landmarks the imaging reveals, used to place a third area between them. Nothing here operationalises IOS. Found by the neighbour query (Q-400). Q-418. — the field of view is placed by finding the boundary between two functionally identified areas
span.quote: In order to localize PPC in mice 3 , 6 , we performed intrinsic optical signal (IOS) imaging 28 , 29 to visualize the boundaries between the γ-barrel column in the mouse whisker barrel cortex and the primary visual cortex V1 (see Methods) (Fig. 1C ). This allowed us to select imaging areas in posterior parietal area A 3 , 30 in the lateral parietal association cortex (LPtA) 31 , located in between the somatosensory barrel cortex and V1.

span.label: LPtA —same-as→ PPC
span.note: THE IDENTITY IS EARNED: the anatomical name is matched to the functional one by tracing inputs and outputs, not asserted from coordinates
span.quote: In four mice, we carried out retrograde and anterograde labelling experiments with tracer injections targeted to LPtA. The resulting labelling patterns validated that this region receives axonal projections from known PPC input sites (Fig. 1D ), particularly the thalamic lateral posterior nucleus LP (Fig. 1H,I ) and premotor cortex M2 (Fig. 1E-F ), as well as sends its axons to known PPC output sites, including M2, the dorsal striatum (Fig. 1E–G ) and LP (Fig. 1H,I ) 15 , 32 . Hence, we identify this region between barrel cortex and V1 as part of PPC

span.label: LP —causes→ PPC
span.note: the main thalamic input, and the candidate origin of the omission signal
span.quote: LP, along with the posterior nucleus Po, is the main source of thalamic input to the PPC, which does not receive any direct input from primary sensory thalamus 2 , 52 . Hence, LP/Po could be a potential source for the Catch-trial responses that we have observed in layer 2/3 of the PPC. This could be in turn modulated through the activation of local inhibitory circuits by top-down feedback, potentially from the FEF, providing the prediction signal in the proposed framework of predictive coding

span.label: M2 —causes→ LPtA
span.quote: In four mice, we carried out retrograde and anterograde labelling experiments with tracer injections targeted to LPtA. The resulting labelling patterns validated that this region receives axonal projections from known PPC input sites (Fig. 1D ), particularly the thalamic lateral posterior nucleus LP (Fig. 1H,I ) and premotor cortex M2 (Fig. 1E-F ), as well as sends its axons to known PPC output sites, including M2, the dorsal striatum (Fig. 1E–G ) and LP (Fig. 1H,I ) 15 , 32 . Hence, we identify this region between barrel cortex and V1 as part of PPC

span.label: RETRACTED (THE TWO ARE ANATOMICAL LANDMARKS IN A METHODS SENTENCE) · barrel cortex —contrasted-with→ V1
span.note: RETRACTED: THE TWO ARE ANATOMICAL LANDMARKS IN A METHODS SENTENCE. The span describes intrinsic optical signal imaging performed 'to visualize the boundaries between the y-barrel column in the mouse whisker barrel cortex and the primary visual cortex V1' IN ORDER TO LOCALIZE PPC. Barrel cortex and V1 are named as the two edges of a region being found. Proximity is not aboutness (Q-190). — the imaged area is DEFINED as what lies between them
span.quote: In order to localize PPC in mice 3 , 6 , we performed intrinsic optical signal (IOS) imaging 28 , 29 to visualize the boundaries between the γ-barrel column in the mouse whisker barrel cortex and the primary visual cortex V1 (see Methods) (Fig. 1C ). This allowed us to select imaging areas in posterior parietal area A 3 , 30 in the lateral parietal association cortex (LPtA) 31 , located in between the somatosensory barrel cortex and V1.

span.label: mismatch —is-a→ omission
span.note: and the paper immediately marks the difference: the MMN paradigms are not this paradigm
span.quote: Indeed stimulus-omission responses have also been described in the auditory 42 , 43 and visual systems 44 – 46 in the context of mismatch negativity (MMN) and oddball responses. However, the stimulus presentation paradigms employed in MMN are different compared to those used in our study.

span.label: predictive coding —operationalised-as→ LP
span.note: offered as a framework for where a prediction signal could come from, not tested
span.quote: LP, along with the posterior nucleus Po, is the main source of thalamic input to the PPC, which does not receive any direct input from primary sensory thalamus 2 , 52 . Hence, LP/Po could be a potential source for the Catch-trial responses that we have observed in layer 2/3 of the PPC. This could be in turn modulated through the activation of local inhibitory circuits by top-down feedback, potentially from the FEF, providing the prediction signal in the proposed framework of predictive coding

span.label: expectancy —causes→ looming
span.note: offered as a reading of the Catch-only and playback responses - 'could potentially represent', so weighted as a proposal
span.quote: Hence, in the Catch-only trials (Fig. 5A ) as well as in the audio playbacks of the looming-like auditory cue (Supplementary Fig. S2 ) the Catch-trial responses could potentially represent a neural correlate of expectancy, here for a potential touch event.

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
span.quote: Non-parametric tests were performed for all analyses, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank paired test and the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test for paired and unpaired group comparisons respectively and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for single distributions.

span.label: Mann-Whitney U test
span.quote: Non-parametric tests were performed for all analyses, and the Wilcoxon signed-rank paired test and the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test for paired and unpaired group comparisons respectively and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for single distributions.

span.label: repeated-measures ANOVA
span.quote: Active neurons were identified by two-way ANOVA with repeated measures of the neuronal calcium signal against the neuropil signal, defined by all pixels not assigned to neuronal soma of the overall ROI annotation

span.label: general linear model
span.quote: A general linear model (GLM) was used to fit the neuronal calcium transients and classify neurons based on their responses 60 , 61 .

span.label: ROC analysis
span.quote: To quantify single-neuron discrimination performance we resorted to a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.

span.label: area under the curve
span.quote: Discrimination performance was then summarized as the obtained area under the curve (AUC).

span.label: permutation test
span.quote: Statistical significance was assessed by a Monte Carlo permutation test

span.label: support vector machine classification
span.quote: We trained linear support vector machine (SVM) classifiers to decode texture graininess (P100 vs. P1200) and texture omission from single trial population activity.

span.label: held-out test set validation
span.quote: Classification performance was assessed by measuring the accuracy on the remaining 50% of the trials that resulted from the initial split of the dataset and were held aside during training.

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: All data are presented as mean ± s.e.m. unless stated otherwise.

span.label: coefficient of determination
span.quote: We obtained an average R 2 value of 0.10

span.label: percentiles
span.quote: Box plots represent the median, the 25 th and 75 th percentiles in the boxes, whereas the sidebars represent the 5 th and 95 th percentiles of the distribution.

span.label: significance level
span.quote: A regression coefficient was considered significantly deviating from baseline β 0 when the corresponding p-value was below a significance level of α = 0.01.

span.label: Wilcoxon signed paired test
span.quote: We found that the peak amplitudes of the evoked responses in Catch-responsive neurons were comparable at the beginning and end of the imaging session (Fig. 3A,B ; peak ∆ R/R : first 5 trials 9.3 ± 2.4%, last 5 trials 12.1 ± 2.5%; p = 0.75; n = 17 Catch-responsive neurons in 4 FOVs, Wilcoxon signed paired test).

span.label: Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test
span.quote: The Catch-trial response showed a significant increase (touch-stimulus peak ∆ R/R : Catch-only trials 3.6 ± 0.7%, interleaved trials 5.2 ± 0.5%; p = 4.8 × 10 −5 , n = 74 neurons, Wilcoxon signed paired test) after tactile experience with 14.9% of active neurons displaying a significant change in activity within this window (8 cells with an increase, 3 cells with a decrease; significance level set at p < 0.01, Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test).

span.label: ROC analysis
span.quote: We carried out an ROC analysis to identify the fraction of neurons that could significantly discriminate between the two presented textures as well as the fraction of neurons that could discriminate between texture-presentation and Catch-trials (compared to shuffled controls, Methods; example traces in Fig. 4B ). Among the trial-active PPC neurons 7.2% (9/126) discriminated between the graininess of the presented textures whereas 17.5% (22/126) discriminated between texture presence and omission

span.label: support vector machine (SVM) classifier
span.quote: As a complement to the ideal observer ROC analysis, we trained a linear support vector machine (SVM) classifier to decode texture graininess and texture omission from single-trial population activity, on a frame by frame basis. This simple readout model could effectively decode texture graininess and texture omission during the touch-stimulus window with about 55% and 70% accuracy, respectively (Fig. 4E ). The decoding accuracy was improved when the mean of the touch-stimulus window was used (60.1 ± 3.1% for texture graininess; 73.1 ± 4.3% for texture omission).

span.label: Layer 2/3 PPC neurons split into subgroups that respond to the auditory cue, to the texture touch, to both, or that are suppressed during cue and texture presentation.
span.quote: PPC neurons displayed a diversity of trial-related responses with some neurons responding to the auditory cues, to the texture stimuli, or both, while others showed suppressed activity during cue and texture presentation

span.label: About 30% of trial-active PPC neurons fired to the omission of the texture touch that normally followed the auditory cues.
span.quote: More interestingly, we found that about 30% of trial-active PPC neurons responded to the omission of the texture touch that always arrived after the auditory cues.

span.label: More than twice as many neurons discriminated texture presence from omission (17.5%) as discriminated the two texture grades from each other (7.2%).
span.quote: Among the trial-active PPC neurons 7.2% (9/126) discriminated between the graininess of the presented textures whereas 17.5% (22/126) discriminated between texture presence and omission

span.label: Omission responses were already present on the very first Catch-trial, which was only the second trial of the session, so PPC encodes the omission without training.
span.quote: Furthermore, for all 4 FOVs the first Catch-trial was presented as the second trial in the sequence of trials, suggesting that the PPC is able to rapidly encode the omission of the auditory-cued tactile stimulus.

span.label: Omission response amplitude did not change between the first five and last five Catch-trials of a session, i.e. it was stable rather than learned over the session.
span.quote: This suggests that PPC neurons are able to report the omission of the texture reliably and stably over time.

span.label: Omission responses occurred with and without whisking, so they are not merely an efference copy of the whisking motor command, although whisking enlarged them.
span.quote: Catch-trial responses were observed both in the absence and presence of whisking behaviour (see Methods) during the touch-stimulus window, indicating that they were not solely dependent on whisking

span.label: Omission responses began before the tone that signalled the stage coming to rest, ruling out the stop tone as their cause.
span.quote: This indicates that the Catch-trial responses were not due to the stop auditory tone and could potentially represent an expectancy response that can be further enhanced by whisking.

span.label: Looming-like auditory cues on their own already drove omission-type responses, and pairing them with texture touch both strengthened those responses and recruited additional neurons reporting omission.
span.quote: Our results suggest that while looming-like auditory cues alone can evoke responses in the PPC, coupling with tactile stimuli enhances this response and further recruits more neurons within PPC that can report subsequent texture-touch omissions.

span.label: A linear classifier read texture omission out of single-trial population activity far better than texture graininess (about 70% versus about 55% accuracy).
span.quote: This simple readout model could effectively decode texture graininess and texture omission during the touch-stimulus window with about 55% and 70% accuracy, respectively

span.label: Only 7.2% of PPC neurons could tell the two sandpaper grades apart, which the authors attribute to the mice being naive, untrained and unrewarded on the texture distinction.
span.quote: Few PPC neurons (7.2%) were able to discriminate the two distinct textures presented.

span.label: Playback of the recorded looming sound reproduced Catch-like responses whereas a non-looming recording did not, isolating the looming quality of the cue as the driver.
span.quote: In a separate set of experiments in these mice, we were also able to evoke Catch-trial like responses in neurons when presented with the audio playback of the looming-like auditory cue but not when presented with a non-looming recording

span.label: about 30 percent of trial-active neurons responded when the cued texture touch was omitted
span.quote: To our surprise, a subset of these ‘unclassified’ neurons (12 out of 46) as well as a subset of classified neurons (26 out of 80) showed a significant response in the touch-stimulus window during Catch-trials, when the texture was omitted (see for example average traces of neurons 1, 3 and 5, Fig. 2A ). We call these special neurons ‘Catch-responsive’ neurons (see Methods), which overall made up 30.2% of the active neurons

span.label: 55.3 percent of those omission-responsive neurons were non-responsive to or suppressed by the texture itself
span.quote: Interestingly, 55.3% of the Catch-responsive neurons were non-responsive or even suppressed during texture presentation trials, suggesting that they were inhibited by the looming-like auditory cues and/or a subsequent texture touch, but relieved from inhibition when the texture was absent.

span.label: the trial-active neurons split by GLM into cue-responsive, touch-responsive, mixed, suppressed and unclassified
span.quote: Using a general linear model (GLM) to fit neuronal calcium traces, we classified the trial-active neurons (n = 126) as cue-responsive (22.2%), touch-responsive (11.9%), mixed-responsive (11.9%) and suppressed (17.5%) based on the dynamics of their calcium responses to the trial period; the remaining 36.5% of ‘unclassified’ active neurons responded neither to auditory cues nor to texture presentation

span.label: 126 of 358 neurons were active during trials, imaged across 13 fields of view in 4 mice
span.quote: We acquired imaging data from 13 fields of views (FOVs) in 4 mice, recording calcium signals in a total of 358 neurons. About 35% of neurons (126/358) were active during the trials

span.label: the omission response was as large at the end of a session as at the beginning, p = 0.75
span.quote: We found that the peak amplitudes of the evoked responses in Catch-responsive neurons were comparable at the beginning and end of the imaging session (Fig. 3A,B ; peak ∆ R/R : first 5 trials 9.3 ± 2.4%, last 5 trials 12.1 ± 2.5%; p = 0.75; n = 17 Catch-responsive neurons in 4 FOVs, Wilcoxon signed paired test).

span.label: LEARNING EXCLUDED BY WHEN IT FIRST APPEARS: the first Catch-trial was the SECOND trial of the session in all four fields of view
span.quote: Furthermore, for all 4 FOVs the first Catch-trial was presented as the second trial in the sequence of trials, suggesting that the PPC is able to rapidly encode the omission of the auditory-cued tactile stimulus.

span.label: the motor-copy account was tested: omission responses occurred with and without whisking, so they are not solely dependent on it
span.quote: We next verified whether the Catch-trial responses might reflect an efferent copy of a motor command such as whisking because the PPC has strong reciprocal connections with the motor and premotor cortices 1 – 3 . Catch-trial responses were observed both in the absence and presence of whisking behaviour (see Methods) during the touch-stimulus window, indicating that they were not solely dependent on whisking

span.label: whisking did enhance the response, 16.4 against 10.1 percent
span.quote: A comparison of the peak of the Catch-trial responses in the presence and absence of whisking during this time window revealed that the response was enhanced by whisking (Fig. 3D ; peak ∆ R/R : whisking 16.4 ± 1.4%, non-whisking 10.1 ± 1.0%; p = 1.47 × 10 −7 , n = 34 Catch-responsive neurons in 12 FOVs, Wilcoxon signed paired test; whiskers could not be tracked in one of the 13 FOVs).

span.label: but response onset time did not differ with whisking, 3.7 against 3.8 s
span.quote: However, the onset time of the Catch-trial responses (from trial start) were comparable in the presence and absence of whisking (Fig. 3E ; Catch-response onset time: whisking 3.7 ± 0.1 s, non-whisking 3.8 ± 0.1 s; p = 0.56, n = 34 Catch-responsive neurons in 17.3 ± 0.1% and 82.7 ± 0.1% of Catch-trials respectively, Wilcoxon signed paired test).

span.label: ACOUSTIC CONFOUND KILLED BY TIMING: omission responses began about 580 ms before the stage stop tone
span.quote: Apart from one neuron (onset 120 ms after the texture stop tone) the others displayed onset times well before the translation stage came to rest (onset 580 ± 65 ms before texture stop tone, n = 18 neurons). This indicates that the Catch-trial responses were not due to the stop auditory tone and could potentially represent an expectancy response that can be further enhanced by whisking.

span.label: omission responses in the touch window were about twice the size of the texture-touch responses
span.quote: Catch trial responses in the touch-stimulus window were larger compared to their corresponding texture-touch responses (Fig. 3G ; peak ∆ R/R : P100 4.5 ± 1.0%, P1200 5.5 ± 0.7%, Catch 10.1 ± 1.0%; p = 1.72 × 10 −5 for P100 vs Catch, p = 4.66 × 10 −5 for P1200 vs Catch; n = 34 Catch-responsive neurons in 12 FOVs; Wilcoxon signed paired test).

span.label: 7.2 percent of active neurons discriminated the two textures while 17.5 percent discriminated presence from omission
span.quote: We carried out an ROC analysis to identify the fraction of neurons that could significantly discriminate between the two presented textures as well as the fraction of neurons that could discriminate between texture-presentation and Catch-trials (compared to shuffled controls, Methods; example traces in Fig. 4B ). Among the trial-active PPC neurons 7.2% (9/126) discriminated between the graininess of the presented textures whereas 17.5% (22/126) discriminated between texture presence and omission

span.label: a population decoder read out graininess at about 60 percent and omission at about 73 percent
span.quote: As a complement to the ideal observer ROC analysis, we trained a linear support vector machine (SVM) classifier to decode texture graininess and texture omission from single-trial population activity, on a frame by frame basis. This simple readout model could effectively decode texture graininess and texture omission during the touch-stimulus window with about 55% and 70% accuracy, respectively (Fig. 4E ). The decoding accuracy was improved when the mean of the touch-stimulus window was used (60.1 ± 3.1% for texture graininess; 73.1 ± 4.3% for texture omission).

span.label: THE CUE DECOUPLED FROM THE TOUCH: three further naive mice received Catch-only trials before any texture was ever presented
span.quote: To verify this possibility, we presented an additional 3 naïve mice first with Catch-trials only, effectively decoupling the auditory cues from tactile stimuli.

span.label: 10 of 74 neurons already responded in the Catch-only condition, and 8 further neurons became responsive only after textures were introduced
span.quote: Indeed, 10 out of the 74 active neurons displayed Catch-responses in the Catch-only trials, as identified using the GLM (see Methods). Eight of these neurons were also Catch-responsive in the interleaved trials (‘pre-existing’ Catch responses) whereas 2 neurons were not classified as Catch-responsive anymore (‘silenced’ responses; Fig. 5A,B ). In addition, 8 other neurons were identified as Catch-responsive only after the introduction of tactile stimuli but not in the Catch-only condition

span.label: CATEGORIES NAMED AND THEN DECLINED: the three subsets are not claimed as functionally distinct groups because the numbers are too low
span.quote: Due to the low numbers of Catch-responsive neurons detected, however, more data would be required to determine if these three subsets of neurons represent functionally distinct groups.

span.label: coupling sound to touch significantly increased the omission response, 3.6 to 5.2 percent
span.quote: The Catch-trial response showed a significant increase (touch-stimulus peak ∆ R/R : Catch-only trials 3.6 ± 0.7%, interleaved trials 5.2 ± 0.5%; p = 4.8 × 10 −5 , n = 74 neurons, Wilcoxon signed paired test) after tactile experience with 14.9% of active neurons displaying a significant change in activity within this window (8 cells with an increase, 3 cells with a decrease; significance level set at p < 0.01, Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test).

span.label: so looming sound alone evokes the response, and coupling with touch enlarges it and recruits more neurons
span.quote: Our results suggest that while looming-like auditory cues alone can evoke responses in the PPC, coupling with tactile stimuli enhances this response and further recruits more neurons within PPC that can report subsequent texture-touch omissions.

span.label: THE RIVAL STATED WITH ITS OWN BEST EVIDENCE CONCEDED: more than half of these neurons did not respond to texture at all, which is what an acoustic account predicts
span.quote: An alternative interpretation is that Catch-responsive neurons are actually acoustically driven and the presence of texture touches merely suppresses their response. Indeed, more than half of Catch-responsive neurons did not respond to or were suppressed by texture touches. However, these Catch-trial responses had onset times well before the tone signalling stage stop (with the exception of one neuron), suggesting that something else than sound, such as the expectancy of an incoming object, evoked the increase in activity.

span.label: and then answered: sensory experience changed the number of omission-responsive neurons, which a fixed sensory response should not do
span.quote: Our results argue against this notion, however, because sensory experience led to changes in the number of Catch-responsive neurons in subsets of PPC neurons, which should not be the case for a reliable sensory response.

span.label: playback of the recorded looming cue evoked the response while a non-looming recording did not
span.quote: We were also able to evoke Catch-trial like responses in neurons when presented with a playback of this auditory looming-like cue, and not with a non-looming recording in mice with previous tactile experience, effectively eliminating other potential unaccounted stimulus sources for the evoked response.

span.label: THE CONFOUND CANNOT BE REMOVED: the looming cue is generated by the texture presentation apparatus itself
span.quote: Unfortunately, we were unable to remove the looming-like auditory cue, as it is an integral part of the texture presentation apparatus.

span.label: retrograde and anterograde labelling validated that this region receives projections from known PPC input sites and sends axons to known PPC output sites, which is why it is identified as part of PPC
span.quote: In four mice, we carried out retrograde and anterograde labelling experiments with tracer injections targeted to LPtA. The resulting labelling patterns validated that this region receives axonal projections from known PPC input sites (Fig. 1D ), particularly the thalamic lateral posterior nucleus LP (Fig. 1H,I ) and premotor cortex M2 (Fig. 1E-F ), as well as sends its axons to known PPC output sites, including M2, the dorsal striatum (Fig. 1E–G ) and LP (Fig. 1H,I ) 15 , 32 . Hence, we identify this region between barrel cortex and V1 as part of PPC

span.label: the cue's looming quality was verified by recording sound at the position of the animal's head
span.quote: We confirmed that the auditory cue generated by the stage translation was indeed looming-like by performing sound recordings at the location corresponding to the head of the head-fixed mouse

span.label: weak texture discrimination is attributed to naive untrained animals with no context attached to graininess
span.quote: Few PPC neurons (7.2%) were able to discriminate the two distinct textures presented. This low discrimination power is not surprising as the experimental sessions were only the second time that the naïve mice were exposed to these textures (the first being setting the texture stop position, prior to imaging start). No explicit association of a relevant context to the texture graininess as stimulus feature or any reinforcement training had been applied.

span.label: both accounts of the omission response turned out to hold: rapid binding in some neurons and direct cue-driving in others
span.quote: This was observed in the very first Catch-trial, suggesting that these neurons either are capable of rapid stimulus binding and association 36 or that they respond directly to the auditory cues generated by the stage translation. We found evidence for both, as Catch-responsive neurons were observed in both the initial Catch-only trials prior to texture touch as well as emerging later in another set of neurons in the subsequent series of interleaved trials.
